rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: ETH remains the single best all-in: the ETF-flow reversal that took hold last week is still accelerating and still ETH-led. US spot-ETHER ETFs added ~$96M in the first three days of last week (heavily concentrated in BlackRock's low-fee ETHA), and CoinDesk's read for the week was explicit — 'Ether outruns Bitcoin as ETF money returns, almost all of it from BlackRock's fund.' On top of the spot bid, BlackRock's ~$100M staked-ETH (ETHB) launch builds a yield-bearing, structural demand source less sensitive to short-term swings. The macro backdrop turned supportive too: a dovish shift from Fed Chair Warsh plus a five-day BTC-ETF inflow streak drove a broad relief bounce, and ETH is the momentum leader within it — up from ~$1,844 (yesterday's entry) to ~$1,871 while BTC/SOL bounced more modestly. Entry ~$1,871 still sits below the $1,900/$1,920 shelf, so the asymmetric 'fresh catalyst + relative strength with a definable stop' setup the mandate prefers is intact.
positions.driver: Re-up ETH — it owns the freshest catalyst (accelerating BlackRock-led ETF inflows + a building staking-ETF demand base) and the clearest relative strength (outrunning BTC and SOL on the bounce), with momentum turning up. Entry $1,871.16 below the $1,900/$1,920 shelf keeps the payoff asymmetric: reclaiming $1,900 opens a run at the 100-day EMA ~$1,943 and beyond, while the ~$1,780 support that pinned it for weeks defines the invalidation. Runners-up rejected: BTC (~$64,440) — flow leader on absolute dollars and lower-beta protection, but no fresh idiosyncratic catalyst and ETH is outperforming it; SOL (~$76.06) — relief-bounce participant but no ETH-grade catalyst for this book and already held in the sister Moonshot-All book.
positions.risks: ETH's strength is concentrated in a few large ETF tickets (BlackRock ETHA/ETHB) rather than broad participation, so the bid can thin fast, and it remains CAPPED below key EMAs (100-day ~$1,943) with repeated stalls at $1,900/$1,920 — a failure there is a live sell-the-news/stretched setup. As the higher-beta major, ETH falls harder than BTC if the relief bounce fades on hawkish surprises, geopolitical shocks, or an ETF-flow flip back to BTC (daily flows are noisy). Hard stop $1721.47 (-8%, majors rule) set with wick room below the ~$1,780 thesis-invalidation support — a clean close under $1,780 means the trade is wrong regardless of the stop.
